title: Proximity effects of chiral magnetization on transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers
authors: Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Igor S. Krivenko, Dmitry S. Smirnov
abstract: We consider the proximity effects of a commensurate chiral $120^{\circ}$ Néel magnetic structure on the transport and optical properties of a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer (TMD ML). The enlarged magnetic unit cell leads to the folding of the Brillouin zone and enables efficient intervalley spin-flip scattering. Starting from a six band tight binding model, we develop an effective $k\cdot p$ model, which describes the coupling between charge carriers in the TMD ML and the chiral magnetization. We predict the anomalous antiferromagnetic Hall effect (AHE) for conduction electrons and describe it accounting for the interplay between anomalous velocity, side jump, and skew scattering contributions. The proximity of the chiral magnetization also leads to the mixing and splitting of the exciton resonances in the two valleys which are related by the time reversal symmetry despite zero net magnetization. Finally, we demonstrate the possibility to measure the distribution of in-plane orientation of the chiral magnetization through Faraday rotation and the ellipticity of incident linearly polarized light.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how coupling a TMD monolayer to a chiral antiferromagnet alters its electronic and optical behavior. Using an effective $k\cdot p$ model, the authors predict measurable effects like the Anomalous Hall Effect and exciton resonance splitting. These predictions allow for potential experimental detection via magneto-optical measurements of the magnetization orientation.
main_problem: The study investigates how proximity effects from a chiral $120^\circ$ Néel magnetic structure modify the transport and optical properties of Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers.
main_result: The proximity effect induces an Anomalous Antiferromagnetic Hall Effect (AHE) and causes splitting/mixing of exciton resonances, even in the absence of net magnetization.
method: The authors developed an effective $k\cdot p$ model derived from a six-band tight binding approach to calculate transport coefficients and optical transition matrix elements.
model_or_system: The system is a TMD ML coupled to a chiral magnet, modeled using an effective Hamiltonian that incorporates exchange interaction, spin-orbit coupling, and symmetry-breaking terms. The analysis focuses on the electronic structure near $K_{\pm}$ and $\Gamma$ points.
key_observables: Anomalous Antiferromagnetic Hall Effect (AHE) conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), splitting of exciton resonances, Faraday rotation ($	heta_F$), and ellipticity ($	heta_E$).
important_parameters: The dependence on the magnetization orientation angle $\varphi$ via a $\cos 3\varphi$ term is crucial for diagnostics.
main_assumptions: The magnetic layer interaction is treated perturbatively to derive the effective $k\cdot p$ model, and certain exchange interactions are neglected for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Brillouin zone folding due to magnetism, energy dispersion curves for pristine TMD bands, and theoretical predictions for magneto-optical responses.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and Hamiltonian (tight binding $ightarrow k\cdot p$ model) to calculating transport properties (AHE via Berry curvature) and finally analyzing optical response (exciton splitting and polarization measurements).
why_interesting: This work connects magnetism, topology (Berry curvature), and low-dimensional materials physics, providing theoretical tools for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in hybrid systems.
